Ipson voted in favor of SB 297, which allowed government officials to opt-out of performing same-sex marriages based on religious objections.

S.B. 200 — Redistricting Amendments. Senate Sponsor: Sen. Curtis S. Bramble. House Floor Sponsor: Rep. Carol Spackman Moss. Senate passed 3/3/2020 with a vote of 25 yes, 0 no, 4 absent. The bill modified Utah Code sections related to redistricting procedures and state procurement rules.

H.B. 215 — Funding for Teacher Salaries and Optional Education Opportunities. House Sponsor: Rep. Candice B. Pierucci. Governor signed January 28, 2023, effective May 3, 2023. Final Senate vote: 20 yes, 8 no, 1 present/abstaining (January 26, 2023). Bill passed by more than two-thirds margin in both chambers.

The Utah Senate passed HB215 on a vote of 20-8, with the bill sent to Governor Spencer Cox for final approval. Senate floor sponsor Sen. Kirk Cullimore stated: 'To get this kind of support we did both in the House and the Senate is really thrilling.' The bill passed by a two-thirds margin in both chambers, meaning it cannot be challenged by referendum.

H.B. 165 — Federal Law Enforcement Amendments. House Sponsor: Rep. Trevor Lee. Senate Floor Sponsor: Sen. Michael S. Kennedy. Senate vote March 1, 2024: 22 yes, 7 no, 0 absent. The law establishes requirements for federal officers releasing undocumented immigrants within Utah, requiring advance notification to state authorities.

S.B. 59 — Tax Amendments. Bill modifies Utah's income tax rate provisions (sections 59-7-104, 59-7-201, 59-10-104, 59-10-1002.2, 59-10-1042). Don Ipson is listed as a cosponsor of this legislation. Senate passed the bill 22-5-2 on 1/28/2022, then passed concurrence 28-0-1 on 2/10/2022. Governor signed February 12, 2022.

Utah Senate passes more than $160 million income tax cut for Utahns. Senate Bill 59, sponsored by Sen. Daniel McCay and cosponsored by 22 other state senators including Don Ipson, drops the current income tax rate from 4.95% to 4.85%. The bill passed the Senate in a 22-5 vote.

Don L. Ipson (R, SD-029). Notable 2025-2026 vote: S.B. 174 — 'Allows a health provider to choose not to participate in certain activities that violate their religious beliefs or conscience.' Ipson voted YES. Also voted NO on SB248 — 'Expanding State-funded Childcare' (2026).

H.B. 452 — Carbon Capture Amendments. House Sponsor: Rep. Scott H. Chew. Senate Floor Sponsor: Sen. David P. Hinkins. Senate passed 27-0-2 on February 29, 2024. Governor signed March 12, 2024. The bill sets up a mechanism for inspection and long-term monitoring of carbon dioxide injection wells, expanding carbon capture and storage infrastructure in Utah.

Don L. Ipson (R, SD-029) — Freedom Score: 64%. Session scores: 2025-2026: 55%; 2023-2024: 73%; 2021-2022: 67%. Ipson serves on the Senate Transportation, Public Utilities, Energy, and Technology Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Appropriations Subcommittee — Utah's key energy and infrastructure policy bodies.

S.B. 16 — Transgender Medical Treatments and Procedures Amendments. Senate Sponsor: Sen. Michael S. Kennedy. Senate passed on third reading 21-7-1 on January 20, 2023. Governor signed January 28, 2023. The bill bans sex reassignment surgeries and places a moratorium on puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for minors.

Don L. Ipson (R, SD-029) — Notable 2025-2026 votes: Voted NO on SB248 — 'Expanding State-funded Childcare' (Child Care Expansion Act, 2026, sponsored by Sen. Luz Escamilla). Also voted NO on SB258 — 'State-Sponsored Preschool for All' and NO on SB217 [per Freedom Index characterization]. Freedom Score for 2025-2026 session: 55%.

H.B. 394 — Homeless Services Funding Amendments. House Sponsor: Rep. Mark A. Strong. Senate Floor Sponsor: Sen. Don Ipson. The bill relates to funding mechanisms for homeless services in Utah. Senate passed the bill with Don Ipson serving as floor sponsor in the Senate.

S.B. 217 — Children's Health Coverage Amendments, Senate final vote February 24, 2023: 22 yes, 3 no, 4 absent. Senators voting Yes include Don Ipson. The bill created a state CHIP program for children who meet income eligibility but are currently ineligible due to citizenship status, covering approximately 2,000 immigrant children including some without legal status.

Don L. Ipson (R, SD-029) — Freedom Score: 64%. The Freedom Index notes Ipson voted YES on SB174 (health provider conscience exemptions, 2026) and voted NO on SB248 (state-funded childcare expansion, 2026). His overall legislative record reflects support for limited government involvement in health coverage programs.
